heroTitle: What goes into your financial plan.
heroSub: Cash flow, investments, retirement income, protection, taxes, and your estate all affect one another. We look at how those pieces work together and build one plan around what you want your money to support.
clarityBody:
We start by understanding what you want your money to do and what you want the next stage of your life to look like.

That gives us something real to plan around. From there, each part of the financial plan has a job.

liquidity.title: Liquidity & Cash Flow
liquidity.sub: Understanding today and planning for what comes next.
paras: Cash flow gives us a clear picture of how your money is working today. We look at income, spending, saving, debt, and the cash you need available for the things you know are coming.

From there, we look ahead. We call the income your plan is designed to support over time your Future Cash Flow. We build a year-by-year picture of where that income may come from and how your savings and investments can help support it.
We also look at how much should remain available in cash so you have flexibility without keeping more on the sidelines than your situation calls for.
walkaway: A clear picture of where your money is going today
A plan for where it's going from here, year by year
The right amount of cash and liquidity for the life you live
A foundation the rest of your financial life can actually stand on

protection.title: Protection
protection.sub: Planning for the risks that could change the plan.
paras: Part of financial planning is understanding what could materially affect the plan you have built.

We review the coverage you already have, where there may be gaps, and whether insurance or other resources may make sense. That can include life insurance, disability insurance, long-term care planning, and other coverage that may affect your financial picture.
Any insurance recommendation should have a clear reason for being there and a specific role in the plan.

extra.head: How insurance is handled
paras: If insurance is part of a recommendation, our advisors may help implement it through an affiliated insurance agency. In that separate role, they may receive a commission.
One Life Advisory does not receive insurance commissions. You are free to purchase any recommended coverage through another agent or company.

walkaway: A clear picture of every risk that could affect your plan
Coverage sized to your actual life and the people who depend on you
A review of what you already have and whether it's still working for you
A protection plan built into your overall financial plan — not bolted on the side

retirement.title: Retirement Income
retirement.sub: Turning what you've built into a plan for income.
paras: Retirement brings a different set of financial decisions. Your savings and investments may need to help replace the paycheck you had while you were working.
We look at Social Security, pensions, investment withdrawals, cash reserves, and other income sources that may be available to you. Then we look at how those pieces can work together over time.
We also test the plan under different assumptions for markets, inflation, taxes, spending, and longevity so we can understand where there may be room to adjust.
walkaway: A clear answer to "can I retire when I want to, and how do I know?"
A year-by-year picture of where your income comes from
A coordinated strategy for Social Security, account withdrawals, and other income sources
A plan stress-tested against the things that could go wrong

investments.title: Investments
investments.sub: Built around the job your money needs to do.
paras: Your investment strategy should reflect what the money needs to accomplish, when you may need it, and how much risk makes sense for your situation.
We start with your goals, time horizon, income needs, and comfort with risk. From there, we build and manage the portfolio around the role those investments have in the broader financial plan.
As your life or the plan changes, we can revisit the investment strategy with it.
walkaway: A portfolio built around what your plan actually needs
The right level of risk for the work the money has to do
Investments coordinated with cash flow, taxes, and the rest of your financial life
A clear answer to "why do I own what I own?"

tax.title: Tax-Aware Planning
tax.sub: Considering taxes as part of the decision.
paras: Many financial decisions have tax consequences. We consider those consequences when we evaluate things like retirement withdrawals, Roth conversions, Social Security timing, charitable giving, investment changes, and other planning decisions.

Your CPA or tax professional remains responsible for tax advice and preparing your returns. When it makes sense, we can coordinate with them so the financial planning and tax work are based on the same information.
walkaway: A plan built with the tax impact of every major decision already factored in
Decisions made on a long enough timeline to actually be the right ones
Coordination between your plan and your CPA
A clearer view of what your choices actually cost — not just this year, but over time

legacy.title: Legacy
legacy.sub: Helping the financial pieces reflect your wishes.
paras: Legacy planning starts with understanding who and what you want your money to support.

We review beneficiary designations, account ownership, and how your financial accounts fit with your existing estate documents. We can also help you think through what you want your family to know and how you would like assets handled over time.
Your attorney remains responsible for legal advice and drafting estate documents. We can coordinate with them so the financial pieces of the plan reflect what you are trying to accomplish.
walkaway: A clear picture of who and what you want to take care of, and how
Accounts, beneficiaries, and titling that actually match your wishes
A coordinated plan between your finances and your estate documents
The clarity of knowing the people you love won't be left figuring it out alone

coordinatedHeading: All of these decisions affect one another.
coordinatedBody:
Cash flow can affect investments. Investment decisions can affect taxes. Insurance can change how much risk the rest of the plan needs to carry. Estate decisions can affect how accounts should be owned or who should be listed as a beneficiary.

We look at those decisions together because changes in one area can affect several others.

That is what financial planning looks like to us.
